Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model

Source: R/nb_power.R
mysterycall_nb_power.Rd

Estimates statistical power to detect a target incidence rate ratio (IRR) in a two-group mystery-caller study using a multilevel negative binomial model with physician random intercepts. Uses Monte Carlo simulation because closed-form power formulas for NB GLMMs require unrealistic approximations.

Usage

mysterycall_nb_power(
  n_physicians,
  calls_per_physician = 2L,
  irr = 0.75,
  theta = 2,
  baseline_mean = 21,
  sigma_u = 0.3,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_sim = 1000L,
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

n_physicians

Integer. Number of physicians (clusters) per group.

calls_per_physician

Integer. Number of mystery calls per physician. Default 2L (one Medicaid, one reference insurance).

irr

Numeric. The IRR to detect (e.g. 0.75 means 25% fewer days for the intervention group). Must be positive.

theta

Numeric. Negative binomial dispersion parameter. Higher values mean less overdispersion (Poisson is the limit as theta -> Inf). Use the $theta from a pilot mysterycall_nb_model() fit, or a literature-based estimate. Default 2.0 (moderate overdispersion typical of wait-time data).

baseline_mean

Numeric. Expected mean wait days in the reference group. Default 21 (three weeks).

sigma_u

Numeric. Standard deviation of the physician-level random intercept (on the log scale). Default 0.3 (typical for specialty scheduling).

alpha

Numeric. Type I error rate. Default 0.05.

n_sim

Integer. Number of Monte Carlo simulations. Default 1000L. Use at least 500 for stable estimates; 2000 for publication.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. Default 42L.

Value

A list of class mysterycall_nb_power with elements:

power

Numeric. Estimated power (proportion of simulations with p < alpha).

n_physicians

Integer. Physicians per group.

total_n

Integer. Total observations (2 x n_physicians x calls_per_physician).

irr

Numeric. Target IRR.

theta

Numeric. Dispersion parameter used.

alpha

Numeric. Type I error rate used.

n_sim

Integer. Number of simulations run.

ci

Numeric vector length 2. 95% Wilson CI around the power estimate.

Choosing theta

If you have pilot data, fit mysterycall_nb_model() and use result$theta. Without pilot data, use theta = 1 (high overdispersion, conservative) to theta = 5 (mild overdispersion). Smaller theta -> lower power -> larger required N.

See also

mysterycall_nb_model() for fitting the NB model; mysterycall_poisson_power() for the Poisson power calculation.

Examples

# Detect a 25% reduction (IRR = 0.75) with 36 physicians per group
result <- mysterycall_nb_power(
  n_physicians = 36L,
  irr          = 0.75,
  theta        = 2.0,
  n_sim        = 200L   # use >= 1000 for real analyses
)
print(result)
#> NB Power Analysis
#>   Physicians/group: 36  Total N: 72  Target IRR: 0.75  theta: 2.00
#>   Estimated power: 41.0%  (95% CI: 34.4%-47.9%)  [200 simulations, alpha=0.050]
